name: Dorsal Spinal Cord Lipoma
aliases: Intramedullary Lipoma of the Dorsal Spinal Cord

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Spinal Cord Lipoma

criteria.description: MRI evidence of a well-demarcated, hyperintense mass on T1-weighted images within the dorsal spinal cord consistent with lipomatous tissue
Presence of progressive neurological deficits such as sensory disturbances or motor weakness correlating with lesion location
Exclusion of other spinal cord tumors or malformations through imaging and clinical assessment
Histopathological confirmation of mature adipose tissue if biopsy or surgery performed

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI confirmation of dorsal spinal cord lipoma with compatible neurological symptoms and exclusion of other spinal cord lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Biopsy is rarely required unless diagnosis is uncertain or surgical intervention planned.

pathognomonic.notes: Loss of proprioception and vibration sense in affected dermatomes
searchTerms: loss of touch and position sense
sensory loss in back spinal pathways

pathognomonic.notes: Typically spastic paresis correlating with lesion level

common.symptomName: Back pain localized to lesion site

common.notes: Tingling or numbness in lower extremities

occasional.notes: Loss of voluntary control of bladder or bowel

searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk in lower limbs

occasional.notes: Increased muscle tone below lesion level

rare.notes: Cystic cavitation within spinal cord associated with lipoma
Skin dimples, hairy patches overlying lesion
searchTerms: cutaneous signs of spinal cord issues

imaging: MRI showing hyperintense dorsal intramedullary mass on T1-weighted images consistent with fat
Fat suppression sequences confirming lipomatous nature
Possible spinal cord compression or tethering
other: Histopathology demonstrating mature adipose tissue if biopsy performed
Neurological examination revealing sensory and motor deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Enhancing intramedullary mass on MRI with heterogeneous signal
Infiltrative spinal cord lesion with variable enhancement
Absence of fat signal on MRI
Often associated with cysts or syrinx
Presence of bony or soft tissue defects
Cutaneous markers such as hairy patches or dimples
May be associated with tethered cord syndrome

redFlags: Signs of acute spinal cord compression
New onset bladder or bowel incontinence
references: Takahashi M, et al. Intramedullary spinal cord lipomas: clinical features and surgical outcomes. Neurosurgery. 2018.
Orphanet: Dorsal spinal cord lipoma - ORPHA:645362
Choi JY, et al. MRI characteristics of spinal cord lipomas. AJNR Am J Neuroradiol. 2015.
